title: CGTN and Iran International Agreed on Something. That's Worth Noting.
subtitle: Chinese state media and Saudi-linked anti-Iranian opposition both affirmed US openness to Iran talks — from opposed strategic interests, for opposed reasons
body_md:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Manila on July 23 on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit. The talks produced no visible progress on Ukraine. Rubio said new proposals would be needed after previous frameworks failed. This is the factual baseline that 10 outlets across 7 countries agreed on. Below it, two opposed media systems converged on the same characterization of US diplomatic posture — and their convergence is more revealing than the meeting itself.

[CGTN Politics](https://news.cgtn.com/news/2026-07-22/Rubio-says-US-still-willing-to-negotiate-over-Iran-crisis-1OZfXJh89nq/p.html?UTM_Source=cgtn&UTM_Medium=rss&UTM_Campaign=Politics) led with: "The United States remains willing to negotiate an end to the US-Iran conflict, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday during a meeting with Southeast Asian foreign ministers in Manila." [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202607227127) reported from the opposite position: "US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that Iran was under severe economic and military pressure but the United States would continue targeting its ability to attack commercial shipping while remaining open to a negotiated solution." Chinese state media — which backs Iranian diplomatic standing internationally — and Saudi-aligned anti-regime opposition — which supports maximum pressure on Tehran — both reported the same core message: the US remains open to talks.

The joint conclusion embedded in that convergence is that the "open to diplomacy" message is credible enough for two editorially opposed operations to run it as straight news. Chinese state media would not amplify US diplomatic openness if doing so contradicted Beijing's strategic interests; Iran International would not amplify it if doing so suggested the pressure campaign was faltering. Both ran the message because it served different but compatible interests: CGTN because US openness validates diplomatic paths that might relieve pressure on Tehran; Iran International because Rubio simultaneously "insisted Washington remained open to diplomacy" while the US "intensified its military campaign against Iran after the first confirmed American combat deaths." The dual-track posture — escalate and negotiate simultaneously — is what both outlets confirmed.

The Ukraine dimension of the Manila talks was covered through a sharper lens. [Kyiv Post](https://www.kyivpost.com/post/80942) framed the Rubio-Lavrov meeting as "a shift in US Ukraine diplomacy," noting that "Rubio said Washington may need new proposals after previous approaches failed to win acceptance from both Kyiv and Moscow." [RFE/RL](https://www.rferl.org/a/rubio-ukraine-war-lavrov-meeting-russia/33810551.html) added that "fresh proposals would be needed after previous peace ideas failed." The framing of failure — not progress, not stalemate, but explicit acknowledgment that prior frameworks collapsed — was consistent across Western and Ukrainian-aligned outlets.

[RT](https://www.rt.com/news/643359-lavrov-rubio-meet-manila/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=RSS) was the only outlet to name the specific framework that failed: the "dead Anchorage plan." That phrase — absent from all other coverage — gives a historical label to a concrete collapsed negotiation. RT also framed the meeting as producing "renewed bilateral US-Russia ties," a characterization that no Western outlet offered. [Breitbart](https://www.breitbart.com/politics/2026/07/23/rubio-rebukes-media-cannot-diplomacy-announce-detail/) covered an entirely different thread: Rubio's rebuke of journalists for asking about the closed-door session, quoting him saying "diplomacy collapses when its details are aired at a microphone." The diplomatic secrecy frame — transparency versus operational effectiveness — was Breitbart's angle and no other outlet's.

Israel, which has direct security stakes in any US-Iran settlement, contributed no coverage. Germany and EU partners, significant stakeholders in Ukraine peace terms, are also absent — likely because they folded the Manila meeting into their broader ceasefire coverage frameworks rather than treating it as a standalone diplomatic event.

The underlying question is what "new proposals" means after the "dead Anchorage plan" and whatever preceded it. Rubio acknowledged that both Kyiv and Moscow rejected prior frameworks. The corpus does not record what those frameworks contained or why they failed. The gap between "fresh proposals needed" and any description of what those proposals might be is the space in which this conflict continues to operate.
